title: The Fundamental Principles of Bioethics
audience: Clinical learners applying bioethical principles to AI and patient data
objectives: Identify the four principles of bioethics in a clinical AI privacy case.
Explain conflicts between AI accuracy, patient privacy, harm prevention, and fairness.
Justify which principle should guide hospital policy when re-identification risk exists.
Reflect on rare groups, de-identification limits, and trust in clinical AI.

sections.name: Clinical Case
sections.purpose: Introduce a hospital AI system using de-identified data with re-identification risk.
sections.how_to_use: Read the case and notice the tension between detailed data for accuracy and privacy risks.

sections.name: Bioethical Principles
sections.purpose: Map the case to autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice.
sections.how_to_use: Select all relevant principles, then optionally compare with the example.

sections.name: Principle Conflicts
sections.purpose: Explain ethical tensions around detailed clinical data use.
sections.how_to_use: Describe how improving care can conflict with privacy, harm prevention, and fairness.

sections.name: Precedence
sections.purpose: Practice defending an ethical clinical policy position.
sections.how_to_use: Choose which principle should guide clinicians and hospital policy, then justify the tradeoff.

sections.name: Reflection
sections.purpose: Connect bioethics to patient trust and vulnerable groups.
sections.how_to_use: Reflect on rare demographic groups, privacy safeguards, and questions raised by AI data use.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner through the clinical case, principles, conflicts, precedence, and reflection.
For clinical users, emphasize patient privacy, re-identification, trust, discrimination risks, and population benefit.
Help learners distinguish de-identification from guaranteed anonymity.
